answer: Bind minting to memory bandwidth, not cores or capacity. The mint runs a function capped by how fast data streams through the RAM bus, work stalling on memory rather than arithmetic. A machine has one fixed aggregate bandwidth — an ocean that cannot be widened by adding cores — so running N identities at once makes them contend and each crawls. You cannot shine one fast pass across many heads like a beacon; a farm of a thousand fakes on one box splits the same fixed bandwidth N ways, each head as starved as a juniper on dry rock, so per-head throughput collapses as the swarm grows.
